f.statement: Manufacturers and MAHs shall comply with good pharmacovigilance practice requirements: address the safety needs of patients, healthcare professionals and the public; management commitment to the quality system; assign tasks and responsibilities; continuous quality improvement; allocate resources for proactive, risk-proportionate, continuous and integrated PV; seek evidence on the risk-benefit balance for decision-making; and foster cooperation with the Authority and other stakeholders. f.title: Report unusual lack of efficacy and medication errors on the ADR form
f.statement: All reports of unusual failure in efficacy shall be reported to the Authority by MAHs using the ADR yellow form (First Schedule); medication errors arising in routine clinical practice shall be reported using the same ADR form.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 33-34

f.title: Report suspected ADRs from all sources including studies and programmes
f.statement: Manufacturers and MAHs shall report to the Authority any adverse reactions or events suspected to be associated with their products notified by HCPs, patients or consumers, including reports from post-marketing experience, unsolicited and solicited sources, clinical trials, non-interventional studies and other post-marketing studies and programmes, meeting the reporting and record-keeping requirements of the Regulations.
f.clause: Regulation 37 Reporting by manufacturers and MAHs
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 37(1)-(3)
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

rows.location: Regulation 37 Reporting by manufacturers and MAHs
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Regularly screen internet and digital media for suspected ADRs
f.statement: Every manufacturer and MAH shall regularly screen the internet, including websites, webpages, blogs, vlogs, social networks, internet forums, chat rooms, health portals and digital media, for potential reports of suspected adverse reactions.
f.clause: Regulation 37 Reporting by manufacturers and MAHs
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 37(4)

f.title: Report medical and non-medical source ADRs on time and assess causality
f.statement: Every manufacturer and MAH shall report all suspected adverse reactions from medical and non-medical sources within the times specified in the Regulations, and shall systematically assess the reports to establish their relationship to the product.
f.clause: Regulation 37 Reporting by manufacturers and MAHs
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 37(5)-(6)

f.title: Monitor international and domestic literature and ongoing studies
f.statement: All manufacturers and MAHs shall regularly monitor international and domestic literature and ongoing safety and efficacy studies for adverse reaction reports or relevant safety findings on their products.
f.clause: Regulation 37 Reporting by manufacturers and MAHs
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 37(7)

rows.quote:
regularly monitor international and domestic literature, ongoing safety and

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report serious adverse reactions within 15 calendar days of minimum information
f.statement: All serious adverse reactions associated with the use of a product shall be reported on an expedited basis, as soon as possible and in no case later than 15 calendar days of initial receipt of the minimum information.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 39(1)-(2)

f.title: Report serious suspected ADRs from post-marketing studies on an expedited basis
f.statement: Every serious suspected adverse reaction occurring in any post-marketing study of which the manufacturer is aware shall be reported to the Authority on an expedited basis.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 39(3)

f.title: Re-classify cases on follow-up and restart the clock for follow-up reports
f.statement: A case initially classified as non-expedited qualifies for expedited reporting when follow-up information indicates re-classification; the reporting time begins again for a follow-up report when medically relevant information is received for a previously reported case.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 39(4)-(5)

rows.quote:

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Manage adverse reaction cases to be authentic, accurate, complete and non-duplicative
f.statement: The management of adverse reactions shall follow good case management practice so that reports are authentic, accurate, as complete as possible and non-duplicative.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 39(6)
f.processes: ICSR quality control; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Submit PSURs/PBRERs when imposed as a condition or requested
f.statement: Every MAH shall submit PSURs and PBRERs for its products where this is prescribed as a condition of marketing authorisation, or when requested by the Authority because of PV concerns or a lack of PSURs for an active substance.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 40(1)

rows.quote: Authority periodic safety update and Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports for

f.title: Follow the PSUR submission frequency counted from authorisation
f.statement: PSURs shall be submitted immediately on request or: for products not yet marketed, at least every 6 months after authorisation until placing on the market; for marketed products, at least every six months during the first two years after initial placing on the market, once a year for the following two years and three-yearly thereafter. Submission dates are calculated from the date of authorisation.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 40(2)

rows.deadline: Immediately on request; otherwise 6-monthly for 2 years, yearly for 2 years, then 3-yearly (from authorisation date)

f.title: Include the minimum PSUR content including sales volume and local and foreign ADRs
f.statement: PSURs shall contain at minimum: summaries of benefit and risk data including results of all studies; a scientific evaluation of the risk-benefit balance; sales volume and prescription data with an estimate of the exposed population; and ADR information (local serious and non-serious, foreign serious and non-serious, literature and conference case reports).
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 40(4)

rows.quote:
The periodic safety update reports shall contain at a minimum the
                          following
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Include a critical integrated benefit-risk analysis in the PBRER
f.statement: The PBRER shall contain a comprehensive, concise and critical analysis of known or emerging important risks and emerging important benefits, including new safety and efficacy information, whether new information accords with previous knowledge, an integrated benefit-risk evaluation for approved indications when new safety information emerges, and recommended actions to optimise the benefit-risk profile.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 40(5)

rows.quote:

f.title: Submit PSURs and PBRERs in hard copy and electronic copy
f.statement: PSURs and PBRERs shall be submitted both in hard copy and in electronic (soft) copy.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 40(6)

rows.quote:
The PSUR and PBER reports shall be submitted both in hard copy
                     and soft copy in electronically.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Submit periodic DSURs covering all ongoing and completed studies
f.statement: Every sponsor and MAH shall submit periodic Development Safety Update Reports on drugs under development, including marketed drugs under further study, providing safety information from all ongoing and completed clinical trials and other studies in the review period (Phase I-IV, therapeutic use, manufacturing-change trials and other significant safety findings).
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 41

rows.quote: required to submit to the Authority the periodic Development Safety Update
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Have documented signal detection and investigation mechanisms
f.statement: Every manufacturer and MAH shall have mechanisms for signal detection and investigation: a system to detect and investigate safety issues at any life-cycle stage in a timely manner; written signal detection procedures; documented roles and responsibilities; documented data sources and methods; documented actions taken; changes in knowledge of risks and benefits sent to the Authority and documented; and review of cumulative cases.
f.clause: Regulation 42 Signal detection, identification and management
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 42(2)

f.title: Register post-authorisation studies and monitor study data for benefit-risk impact
f.statement: Post-authorisation studies (which the Authority may impose as a condition) shall be registered under the clinical trials control regulations; the MAH shall monitor data generated during the study and consider implications for the risk-benefit balance.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 43(2)-(3)

rows.quote:

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Communicate new benefit-risk information from studies within 14 days
f.statement: Every new piece of information that may affect the risk-benefit balance shall be communicated immediately, within 14 days, in writing to the Authority as an emerging safety issue; study findings are also provided through PSURs.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 43(4)

f.title: Report study ICSRs and SAEs under the clinical trial regulations
f.statement: Individual cases of suspected adverse reactions and serious adverse events arising from post-authorisation studies shall be reported according to the clinical trials control regulations in force.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 43(6)

f.title: Submit six-monthly PASS progress reports and the final report within 12 months
f.statement: Six-monthly progress reports on the studies shall be submitted, and the final study report within twelve months of the end of data collection.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 43(7)-(8)

f.title: Keep PASS PV obligations auditable and include imposed studies in the RMP
f.statement: The MAH shall ensure fulfilment of its PV obligations in relation to the study can be audited, inspected and verified, and information on studies conducted under an obligation imposed by the Authority shall be included in the RMP.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 43(9)-(10)

f.title: Report medical device adverse events and evaluate device risks
f.statement: MAHs shall report to the Authority all adverse events or incidents associated with use of medical devices and ensure collection, analysis and evaluation of device risks (adverse effects, interactions, contraindications, falsifications, operational and technical defects, malfunctions) and necessary measures, per the medical devices regulations and guidelines.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 44

rows.quote:

rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Report serious undesirable effects of cosmetics within 14 days
f.statement: Manufacturers, MAHs and distributors of cosmetics shall report all known serious undesirable effects, the product name and any corrective measures to the Authority within fourteen days of becoming aware.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 45(1)-(2)

rows.actor: Manufacturers, MAHs and distributors of cosmetics

f.title: Operate cosmetovigilance, take corrective measures and submit annual CPSR
f.statement: For cosmetics, manufacturers and MAHs shall: list products containing a substance under serious safety doubt with concentrations; take appropriate corrective measures, withdrawal or recall within the stated time limit; conduct investigations requested by the Authority; establish a cosmetovigilance and serious undesirable effect management and communication system; submit an annual Cosmetics Product Safety Report for new products with a causality assessment; and undertake corrective actions following post-marketing surveillance data.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 45(4)-(10)

f.title: Report adverse reactions to antiseptics and disinfectants
f.statement: Manufacturers and MAHs shall report adverse reactions associated with antiseptics and disinfectants using the First Schedule form (paper or electronic), under the Regulations' reporting requirements and timelines.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 46

f.title: Report clinical trial SAEs and SUSARs under the Clinical Trials Control Regulations
f.statement: Reporting of serious adverse events and serious unexpected adverse drug reactions in clinical trials shall comply with the Clinical Trials Control Regulations in force.
f.clause: Regulation 47 Adverse events in clinical trials
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 47; GN No. 53 of 2013

f.title: Report suspected falsified or substandard products and conduct extra monitoring on request
f.statement: The MAH shall report suspected falsified or substandard products to the Authority using the Third Schedule form, shall not deal in confirmed substandard or falsified products, and may be required to conduct extra monitoring and submit reports.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics (Pharmacovigilance) Regulations 2018, reg. 48

f.title: Non-compliance can lead to suspension, cancellation and criminal offences
f.statement: The Authority may suspend or cancel registration of products that fail to comply with the Regulations (with or without notice when needed to prevent injury). Contravening the Regulations is an offence, and any person who fails to notify the Authority of adverse reactions and events commits an offence liable to a fine, imprisonment or other legal action under the Act.
